title: Medical Image Classification for Research and Education
description:
Research and education use case. The results are not a medical device and must not be used for diagnosis or other clinical decisions.

Researchers and students who work with X-ray, CT or MRI data need a reproducible starting point for image classification experiments: reading DICOM files correctly, keeping identifying data out of experiments, training a convolutional neural network, and evaluating it with the metrics used in medical imaging studies. The goal is a small, transparent pipeline that classifies images into two classes (for example "finding" and "no finding") on a public or approved dataset and makes it easy to inspect what the model looks at.

Requirements

  • Read DICOM pixel data with correct rescaling, windowing and photometric interpretation.
  • Remove direct identifiers before images are used in an experiment.
  • Train on a CPU for small experiments and on a GPU with transfer learning for larger ones.
  • Report sensitivity and specificity on a held-out test set.
  • Show heatmaps of the image regions that drive the output.

Constraints

  • Only data with suitable licenses and approvals; storage and processing that meet data-protection rules (for example GDPR, HIPAA).
  • Splits by patient, not by image, to avoid overly optimistic results.
  • Clinical use would require validation and regulatory clearance as a medical device, which is out of scope.
goals:
• The full pipeline (DICOM loading, training, evaluation) runs end to end on a public dataset with one command.
  • Sensitivity and specificity reported with confidence intervals on a patient-level held-out split.
  • Grad-CAM heatmaps reviewed for a sample of test images to check for shortcuts such as text markers.
  • No direct patient identifiers in any file used for training.
